Quick update — I ran 3 model variations in infra_econ_model_v3.xlsx:

A) Conservative: no additional reserved capacity, rely on current autoscale + conservative burst (cost baseline)
B) Reserve+Hedge: purchase 15% reserved capacity for Q3 + 30% cheap burst buffer (moderate cost, higher SLA)
C) Surge Simulation: assume 4x weekend spike (per Pete); simulate slot pre-provisioning + aggressive kvcache TTLs

Topline outputs (all in model's 'Summary' tab):
- Expected monthly GPU spend range: $2.1M (Conservative) -> $2.9M (Reserve+Hedge) under baseline demand
- If quantize to 4-bit broadly in production, model shows a theoretical token-cost reduction of ~22% vs FP16, but we modeled only 12% realized reduction due to quality guardrails.
- Under the 4x spike C) with a 15% reserved hedge + 30% burst, expected peak spend for spike weeks rises to $4.6M/week; amortized across the month that becomes a ~+38% uplift.

I've added an assumptions sheet and a short list of items I'd like Product to confirm (latency SLOs per route, percent of traffic eligible for kvcache). Drive link has raw outputs.

Karthik
